item.title: I need to talk about this.
item.description:
Please allow me to word vomit my thoughts on a subject that is very near to me. 1) My friend and I had ridden to the peak of the same mountain on the same day, to celebrate my birthday a day early, and left the top just about 15 minutes before the torrential hail (that literally came in visible waves) and the singular lightning strike. (We had made it almost back to the Summit Lake Area and immediately ran in to the bathrooms for shelter, but we were already soaked.) I jumped when the lightning hit, because it seemed very close to my motorcycle, and I immediately thought that someone had probably just died, since the peak was crowded with people. 2) Incidentally, I knew this kid's family, we used to be close enough to spend holidays together, though I haven't seen them since Levi was about 5. I went to his parent's wedding in Oregon, and I was in the dad's bible study since around Y2K. 3) the parents have been seasonal missionaries to Africa since shortly after they married. They are both amazing, selfless, incredibly generous people. I am so sad for them. 4) I used to be a devout evangelical, but logic and reading the bible completely several times cured me of that, which is kinda when I lost regular communication with the family. Regardless, 5) I am horrified that the folks in the comments have turned it into a "he knew Jesus, so he's ok" vs Facebook atheists argument. Both arguments at this hour are incredibly insensitive to the family, his three remaining brothers (one was air lifted to Denver and is still in ICU), who at some point in the future may read all the comments. 6) as a pedantic bitch, it pisses me off that more of the bullshit in the comments is over the goddamn name of the mountain than the kids. It used to be called Mt Evans. John Evans was the territory governor who incited the SAND CREEK MASSACRE in 1864, so it was decided that a genocidal asshole shouldn't be honored, and they let the local tribes pick the new name. Get over it, losers. 7) a little part of me (my inner atheist) is saying how crazy it is that, if there were a God, that such an amazing, kind, loving, and most importantly, devout family could be literally struck down like Job, and what a crappy religion it is that allows people to justify stuff like this as coming from a "just and loving God." 8) the childish/selfish part of me is mad that I did this major thing (that road is fucking terrifying to ride a motorcycle up, with 19 switchbacks/hairpin turns and a very loose definition of the word "paved"), and I can't be happy about that publicly anymore. I feel like an asshole.
I took this video right before leaving the peak. That is the storm in question.
A pile of pea-size hail that happened while we were sheltering in the bathroom.
